id: P:Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo
summary: Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Mio Kishimoto is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1971 to 1979. She held posts at Ochanomizu University (~1979–1994) and served as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1994–2007).
Mipam Chökyi Jampa studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Miranda Shaw was taught by Robert A. F. Thurman, completed doctoral studies under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and was mentored by postdoctoral mentor Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

Mircea Eliade studied at the University of Bucharest and University of Calcutta, completing his doctorate under Surendranath Dasgupta. Working in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, he taught at Bucharest, the EPHE, and Sorbonne, and was professor at the University of Chicago.

Mireille Bénisti worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, earning diplomas at École du Louvre and EPHE under Philippe Stern, Louis Renou, Jean Filliozat, and Paul Mus. She held posts at CNRS, Musées Nationaux, and Phnom Penh.
Mireille Helffer worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She was a Chargé de Recherche at CNRS (~1969–1993) and was affiliated with Paris Nanterre University (attested 1985).

Mirella Keller works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned an MA at Fo Guang University (2015–2018) and a PhD at Eötvös Loránd University (2019), becoming an assistant professor at Dharma Gate Buddhist College in 2025.
Mirella Lingorska is an Indologist and linguist who held posts at the University of Tübingen and as Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich (both attested 2026).

Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the University of Otago and completed a PhD under John A. Baker at the University of Calgary (–2005), later holding posts at UNSW and the University of Western Australia.

Miriam Levering was a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned her PhD at Harvard University in 1978. She was a professor of religious studies at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (attested 2007–2010).

Mirjan Damaška studied at Zagreb, Ljubljana, and the International Faculty of Comparative Law. He held positions at the University of Zagreb, International Faculty of Comparative Law, and the University of Pennsylvania, and taught at Yale Law School from ~1976 to 2011.
Miron Winslow worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Middlebury College (~1813–1815) and Andover Theological Seminary (~1815–1818), and founded the American Madras Mission in 1836.

Miroslav Marcovich studied at the University of Belgrade and worked in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Belgrade, University of Los Andes (1955–1959), and served as Professor of Classics at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1969–1989).
Mitashree Srivastava, who works in Buddhist studies, completed an M.Sc at the University of Allahabad in 2007 and was appointed associate professor at the University of Delhi in 2013.
Mitchell G. Weiss, a specialist in Indology, studied under Ludo Rocher and served as a professor at the University of Basel.

Mithilesh Chaturvedi is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who served in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Delhi (attested 2009) and later as Professor Emeritus there (attested 2026).

Mitsuji Fukunaga studied at Kyoto University and worked in philosophy, sinology, and religious studies. He held posts at Aichi University of Education, Kyoto University (1961–1982), the University of Tokyo (1974–1979), Kansai University (1982–1986), and the University of Kitakyushu (1986–1989).
Mitsukuni Yoshida was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1942–1945) and held a post at Kyoto University of the Arts (~1982–1991).
